question.text: Will at least one additional U.S. state enact a cage-free egg requirement before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before July 1, 2027, a U.S. state without an existing cage-free law in effect as of September 1, 2026, enacts a new cage-free requirement.

A cage-free requirement is a law or rule that either bans the use of cages for in-state hens or bans the sale of eggs from non-cage-free hens.
question.fine_print:
To qualify, a cage-free requirement may be enacted by the state legislature, passed by a ballot measure, or implemented via state administrative action. The requirement need not come into effect before July 1, 2027.

If a state legislature passes a cage-free requirement, that will suffice for this question to resolve as Yes, regardless of the action or inaction of the state's governor.

States with cage-free requirement on the books as of September 15, 2026 are Arizona, California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Michigan, Nevada, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah, and Washington.

research:
Based on my searches, nothing has resolved this yet, and no other state appears close. No new state has enacted a cage-free requirement since about 2021-2022, and recent action has mostly been delays and repeal attempts.

## 1. Resolution source
- There is no single official data series. The question names the 10 states with laws as of 2026-09-15. ASPCA's tracker (undated, ©2026) lists the same 10 states for laying hens, and no others. Maine, New Jersey, Florida, Kentucky and Ohio appear only for pig or calf crates. The page notes "a number of others are currently debating similar laws" but names none. [ASPCA](https://www.aspca.org/improving-laws-animals/public-policy/farm-animal-confinement-bans)
- 2026-11-10: The Humane League says laws have "passed in 10 states" and "proposals are advancing in additional states." It does not name those states. [THL Eggsposé](https://thehumaneleague.org/article/2026-eggspose)

## 2. Current status
- I found no 11th state that has enacted a cage-free law in 2026. Nothing settles the question.
- New York S950 / A652, the most prominent bill, never left the Senate Agriculture Committee. Its last action was a referral on 2026-01-07. The 2025-26 session has ended, so the bill would need to be reintroduced in 2027. NY versions have failed every session since 2019-20. [NY Senate](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/S950)
- Vermont H.4, a 2026-session bill using UEP cage-free space standards, was introduced. I could not confirm its status, but nothing suggests it passed. [VT legislature](https://legislature.vermont.gov/Documents/2026/Docs/BILLS/H-0004/H-0004%20As%20Introduced.pdf)
- I could not find any 2026 cage-free bill in New Jersey, Illinois, Maryland or Delaware, and no 2026 or 2027 ballot initiative.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-09: Nevada SB41 was prefiled for the 2027 session. It would repeal Nevada's limits on confining egg-laying hens. I saw this only in a search snippet, because LegiScan blocked the fetch. [LegiScan](https://legiscan.com/NV/bill/SB41/2027?guid=3BFKP12y2pZLwvAKgrnXNM)
- 2026-06-03: Reports said Congress might roll back state farm-animal welfare rules. [WOWT](https://www.wowt.com/2026/06/03/farm-animal-welfare-rules-might-be-rolled-back-by-congress/)
- 2026-04-30: The House passed a farm bill (224-200) that includes the Save Our Bacon Act, which would preempt state confinement rules. A June report said the Senate Ag Committee would leave this out "for now." I could not verify its final status. [ASPCA](https://www.aspca.org/news/farm-bill-moves-forward-mixed-results-animals)
- 2026-03-18: A federal court dismissed DOJ's challenge to California's egg laws for lack of standing. A similar DOJ suit against Michigan was also dismissed. [Nat Law Review](https://natlawreview.com/article/district-court-rules-doj-has-no-standing-challenge-californias-egg-standards), [Feedstuffs](https://www.feedstuffs.com/policy/judge-rejects-doj-suit-against-michigan-cage-free-egg-law)
- 2026-01-13: A Michigan repeal bill was sent to the Senate Economic Growth Committee. [WHMI](https://whmi.com/news/article/47126)
- 2025: Arizona's governor delayed the state's rule to 2034. The legislature passed a full repeal (SB1721), which she vetoed, according to ASPCA's 2025 recap. Nevada allowed emergency suspension of its sales ban. Cage-free bills in Maryland, New York, Tennessee and Vermont were introduced but not enacted. [ASPCA 2025 recap](https://www.aspca.org/node/69760)

## 4. Base rates
- Laws enacted by year: Massachusetts (2016 ballot), Rhode Island (2018), California Prop 12 (2018; earlier laws in 2008 and 2010), Oregon (2019), Washington sales ban (2019), Michigan sales ban (2019), Colorado (2020), Nevada (2021), Utah (2021), Arizona (administrative rule, 2020-2022). [ASPCA](https://www.aspca.org/improving-laws-animals/public-policy/farm-animal-confinement-bans), [Humane World](https://www.humaneworld.org/en/blog/breaking-news-colorado-becomes-seventh)
- That was about 1-3 new states a year from 2016 to 2021. Since 2022 there have been zero in roughly 4.5 years.
- Since 2024 the direction has reversed. Utah and Rhode Island pushed their deadlines to 2030, Arizona to 2034, and Nevada added a suspension option. This followed bird flu and high egg prices.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on new state cage-free laws.
- The Kalshi markets supplied with this task do not match the question. "Cage-Free" at 0.73 is about whether Cal-Maine says the word on its 2027-01-06 earnings call. The other markets cover egg prices and unrelated policy.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (2027-07-01)
- January to June 2027: Most state legislatures hold their regular sessions. Possible reintroductions include New York, where Democrats hold both chambers, as well as Vermont, Maryland, New Jersey and Illinois. Note that only legislative passage is needed to resolve Yes; a governor's signature is not required.
- 2027 session: Nevada SB41 repeal, plus possible repeal or delay efforts in Michigan, Colorado and elsewhere.
- Federal farm bill: if Senate and House negotiators keep Save Our Bacon-style preemption, it would discourage new state laws.
- Bird flu and egg prices: the UK ordered hens indoors from 2026-11-13 because of rising bird flu cases. A similar rise in US outbreaks would likely keep cage-free costs a political issue. [Mirror](https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/free-range-eggs-bird-flu-37866454)
- Ballot measures cannot help: none are scheduled for a vote before July 2027.

# Will another U.S. state enact a cage-free egg requirement before July 1, 2027? Research summary as of 2026-11-11

So far nothing has happened that settles this question. No state has enacted a new cage-free law since 2021. The pending bills I found are stalled in committee, and the policy momentum since 2025 has gone toward rollbacks, not new laws.

## 1. Resolution source
- There is no single data series that decides this. It comes down to state legislative records, ballot results and agency rules. The question lists 10 states as having laws as of 2026-09-15: AZ, CA, CO, MA, MI, NV, OR, RI, UT and WA.
- 2026-11-03: Arizona's rule may no longer count as "existing." Maricopa County Superior Court Judge Scott Blaney ruled that the Department of Agriculture lacked authority to require cage-free production, and his ruling voids the whole rule. The Attorney General's office says it is "reviewing" the decision, and I found no appeal yet. If Arizona later re-enacts by statute or ballot, it is unclear whether that would count as a "state without an existing law." [KJZZ](https://www.kjzz.org/business/2026-11-03/arizona-judge-rules-against-cage-free-requirements-for-egg-producers)

## 2. Current status
- I found no state that enacted a qualifying law between 2026-09-01 and today.
- Pending bills I could find, none of which has advanced:
  - **New York:** A652 was referred to the Agriculture committee on 2026-01-07, and its Senate companion S950 is also in committee. Both expire when the session ends at the close of 2026. [NY Senate A652](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/A652), [S950](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/S950)
  - **Vermont:** H.4 (2025-26 session) would ban confinement that prevents wing spreading. I found no record of it moving. [VT Legislature](https://legislature.vermont.gov/Documents/2026/Docs/BILLS/H-0004/H-0004%20As%20Introduced.pdf)
  - **Maryland:** advocates keep returning. A Humane World factsheet created 2026-07-22 urges a cage-free bill with a phase-in, which suggests a push in the 2027 session. Earlier bills (SB 806 in 2025, HB 357/SB 193 in 2024) died in committee. [Humane World MD factsheet](https://www.humaneworld.org/sites/default/files/docs/md-factsheet-cage-free-2026.pdf), [MGA SB806](https://www.mgaleg.maryland.gov/mgawebsite/Legislation/Details/SB0806?ys=2025rs), [CNS Maryland 2024](https://cnsmaryland.org/2024/03/13/cage-free-egg-bill-cracks-under-pressure/)
- I found no statewide hen-confinement measure on the November 2026 ballot. Oregon's IP 28 failed to qualify, and it was a broader animal-killing measure anyway. [Food & Water Watch](https://www.foodandwaterwatch.org/2026/07/28/misguided-oregon-ballot-measure-fails-to-qualify/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-10: The Humane League's 2026 Eggsposé report covers corporate pledges only, not state laws. [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/new-report-reveals-major-cage-free-progress-across-us-restaurant-chains-but-some-big-brands-still-fall-short-302933673.html)
- 2026-11-09: Nevada Sen. Robin Titus prefiled SB41 to repeal Nevada's hen-confinement restrictions. [LegiScan](https://legiscan.com/NV/bill/SB41/2027?guid=3BFKP12y2pZLwvAKgrnXNM)
- 2026-11-03: The Arizona ruling described above. Humane World says it will pursue "new legislation or a future ballot measure" in Arizona. [KJZZ](https://www.kjzz.org/business/2026-11-03/arizona-judge-rules-against-cage-free-requirements-for-egg-producers)
- Late 2026: In a year-end Q&A, ASPCA says its farm-animal priority is "preventing hostile efforts to roll back" existing protections. It mentions no new state cage-free wins. [ASPCA](https://www.aspca.org/node/70647)
- 2026-04-30: The U.S. House passed a Farm Bill that includes the Save Our Bacon Act, which would preempt state confinement laws. A DOJ lawsuit against Prop 12's egg provision is also pending. [Humane World Action](https://humaneaction.org/press-release/2026/04/animal-welfare-laws-threatened-farm-bill-passes-us-house-largely-party-line), [Humane World explainer](https://humaneaction.org/press-release/2026/06/whats-happening-california-prop-12-farm-bill-and-save-our-bacon-act)
- 2026-01-13: A Michigan repeal bill was referred to the Senate Economic Growth Committee. [Animal Ag Alliance](https://animalagalliance.org/issues/legislation/)
- 2025: Rollbacks followed high egg prices and bird flu:
  - **Arizona:** Gov. Hobbs delayed the rule to 2034.
  - **Nevada:** a law now allows emergency suspension of its sales ban.
  - **Colorado:** a repeal bill failed. [KJZZ](https://www.kjzz.org/politics/2025-03-21/hobbs-delays-arizonas-cage-free-rules-but-egg-prices-are-unlikely-to-come-down), [Las Vegas Sun](https://lasvegassun.com/news/2025/feb/14/can-suspending-a-cage-free-egg-law-solve-the-soari/), [KUNC](https://www.kunc.org/news/2025-01-28/colorado-lawmakers-reject-attempt-to-roll-back-egg-law)

## 4. Base rates
- The dates below are from my background knowledge. I did not re-verify each one this session.
  - **Enactments:** MA in 2016 (ballot), CA in 2018 (Prop 12, after Prop 2 in 2008), RI in 2018, OR, WA and MI in 2019, CO in 2020, AZ by rule in 2020 (strengthened 2022), UT and NV in 2021.
  - **Pace:** about 9-10 states in 2016-2021, roughly 1.5-2 a year.
  - **Since 2021:** zero new states in about 5 years, through 2022-2026.
- Over the comparable recent window, the rate of new enactments within roughly 8 months is close to zero. In that same period, backlash tied to egg prices and bird flu has dominated.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. The closest Metaculus questions are about cage-free hen share (resolved at 45.43%) and factory-farm ballot measures by 2030. [Metaculus](https://metaculus.com/questions/3344/egg-laying-hens-cage-free-in-us-in-june-2025)
- None of the Kalshi markets supplied with the question matches it. The Cal-Maine earnings-call "Cage-Free" mention market is at 0.73, but it is not relevant to state enactments.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- January to June 2027 sessions, with approximate end dates from my background knowledge rather than checked this session:
  - **Maryland:** session ends around April 2027, and it is the most likely target for advocates.
  - **New York:** new 2027-28 bills would need to be reintroduced, and the session ends around June 2027.
  - **Vermont, Illinois and New Jersey:** possible activity, but I found no specific bills.
- I know of no statewide elections with ballot measures before July 2027.
- A possible Arizona appeal or new Arizona legislation, with the counting ambiguity noted in section 1.
- Farm Bill preemption in the Senate, and the DOJ v. California case. Either could discourage new state laws.
- Repeal fights in Nevada (SB41, 2027 session) and Michigan, which may absorb advocates' resources.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) Time left and what Yes requires: the deadline is July 1, 2027, about 7.5 months away. Almost all realistic opportunities fall in the January-June 2027 legislative sessions. Yes requires that a state without a cage-free law in effect on September 1, 2026 enact one. That means its legislature passes a ban on caging in-state hens or on selling non-cage-free eggs (a governor's signature is not needed), or it adopts such a ban by ballot measure or administrative rule. Arizona had a rule in effect on September 1, 2026, so re-enacting it after the November 2026 court ruling likely would not count.

(b) Status quo: No. No 11th state has acted, and no qualifying bill is currently moving.

(c) Base rate: from 2016 to 2021, about 1.5-2 states a year enacted laws, which would imply a 60-70% chance in a 7.5-month window. From 2022 to 2026, there were zero new states in about 5 years, which implies roughly 0-10% for a single half-year session window. The recent regime is more relevant because the bird-flu and egg-price backlash continues, so I start near 8-10%.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - A Humane World Maryland factsheet (2026-07-22) points to a 2027 push in Maryland, a Democratic trifecta state.
  - New York and Vermont bills are likely to be reintroduced.
  - Legislative passage alone suffices.
  - The Humane League (2026-11-10) says "proposals are advancing in additional states."
- For No:
  - New York's S950/A652 died in committee again in 2026, and New York has failed every session since 2019.
  - Maryland bills died in 2024 and 2025.
  - Vermont's H.4 did not move.
  - The 2025 rollbacks show the political mood: Arizona delayed to 2034 and then saw a repeal veto, Nevada added a suspension option, and Utah and Rhode Island delayed.
  - Repeal efforts continue, with Nevada SB41 prefiled on 2026-11-09 and a Michigan repeal bill pending.
  - ASPCA describes its priority as defense against rollbacks.
  - The House farm bill (2026-04-30) included preemption.
  - No ballot measures are possible before the deadline.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: the 2027 sessions open with high egg prices and bird-flu concerns. Advocates spend their resources defending Nevada and Michigan, and the Maryland and New York bills die in committee again.
- Yes: Maryland's Democratic legislature passes a cage-free bill with a long phase-in (for example, 2032) and industry acquiescence, since many large producers have already converted, before sine die in April 2027.

(f) Adjustment: I start at about 8% from the recent-regime base rate. I adjust down slightly because there are no live bills, the momentum is toward rollback, and federal preemption pressure is building. I keep some weight on Maryland or another blue state as a tail possibility, since only legislative passage is needed. Final estimate: about 6%.

Probability: 6%

**(a) Time left and what Yes requires.** There are about 7.5 months until July 1, 2027. Most of that window covers the January to June 2027 legislative sessions. Yes requires a state with no cage-free law in effect as of September 1, 2026 to enact one, by legislative passage (no governor's signature needed), ballot measure or administrative rule. Arizona already had a rule as of that date, so re-enacting it after the November 3 court ruling likely would not count. Even if it did, a re-enactment is improbable before mid-2027.

**(b) Status quo.** No. No new state has enacted a cage-free law since 2021, and the pending bills (NY S950/A652, VT H.4, past Maryland bills) all died in committee.

**(c) Base rate.** From 2016 to 2021 roughly 1.5 to 2 states a year enacted laws, which would suggest about 60% or more for an 8-month window. The relevant recent regime is different: zero new enactments in roughly 5 years (2022 to 2026), alongside active rollbacks. On that recent regime, the rate for an 8-month window is well under 10%, roughly 5 to 8%.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
- **For Yes:** Advocates appear to be preparing a 2027 Maryland push (Humane World factsheet, July 22, 2026). New York has Democratic trifectas and recurring bills. Only legislative passage is needed, not a signature.
- **For No:**
  - The trend since 2024 to 2025 runs toward delays and repeals: Arizona delayed to 2034 and its rule was later voided by a court on November 3, 2026; Utah and Rhode Island delayed to 2030; Nevada added a suspension option and SB41 to repeal its law was prefiled November 9, 2026; a Michigan repeal bill is pending.
  - Bird flu and egg-price politics persist.
  - House farm bill preemption, passed April 30, 2026, discourages new state laws.
  - ASPCA describes its priority as defending existing laws.
  - No ballot measures are possible before July 2027.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- **No:** The 2027 sessions open with bills reintroduced in NY, MD and VT. Egg industry opposition and price concerns keep them in committee, and advocates spend their resources defending Nevada and Michigan.
- **Yes:** Maryland or Vermont passes a phased-in cage-free bill with a long runway (for example, a 2032 effective date), framed as low-cost because most supply is already transitioning. Both chambers pass it before sessions adjourn in spring 2027.

**(f) From base rate to final probability.** No market covers this question, so there is no market anchor. I start near 6 to 8% from the recent-regime base rate. I adjust down slightly for the clearly negative policy momentum and the absence of any bill with demonstrated traction. I keep some weight on the low bar (passage alone suffices) and on organized advocacy in Maryland, New York and Vermont.
